eventMetadata.context_description:
**Strong southerly winds and persistent showers associated with a polar air mass have kept Wellington’s daytime maximum tightly capped near 10°C on August 16, 2026.** Official MetService guidance and supporting ensemble models from regional agencies consistently project a high of 8–10°C under cloudy, breezy conditions, aligning with the market’s overwhelming 98.6% implied probability for exactly 10°C. Typical August climatology in Wellington features average highs near 12°C, but the current setup—marked by strong southerlies mixing cooler maritime air and limiting insolation—has suppressed temperatures below seasonal norms, as confirmed by recent NIWA and MetService observations of overnight lows around 5°C and limited daytime recovery.  

A realistic challenge would require an unexpected wind shift to northerly or lighter flows combined with earlier clearing, which could allow modest warming toward 11–12°C; however, the latest model runs show low spread and reinforce the southerly regime through the afternoon, leaving little room for deviation before resolution.

**Recent official forecasts from the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) position a maximum of 33°C as the most probable outcome for August 17, 2026.** Multiple sources, including direct HKO-linked regional forecasts and consistent third-party summaries aligned with them, project a daily range of 28–33°C under sunny intervals with scattered showers and squally thunderstorms developing later in the day. Medium-high rain chances introduce cloud cover that can suppress peak afternoon heating, keeping the high near or slightly below the upper end of the forecast.

This follows an extreme heat episode driven by Typhoon Dolphin’s outer subsidence, which produced a record 36.9°C at the HKO headquarters on August 10—the highest since records began in 1884. The influence has since weakened, with the airstream moderating and upper-level disturbances increasing moisture and shower activity. Seasonal outlooks from the HKO note normal-to-above-normal temperatures for August–October overall, consistent with the long-term warming trend, yet the immediate daily pattern favors moderation.

Traders have placed the highest implied probability on 33°C (37.5%), followed closely by 32°C (25.5%) and 34°C (23.0%), reflecting the narrow forecast band and inherent uncertainty from variable shower timing, model consensus, and localized urban effects. Resolution hinges on the official HKO maximum recorded at the headquarters station, where even modest increases in cloud or rainfall can shift the peak by 1°C. No major new tropical systems or abrupt pattern changes are indicated in the latest guidance, supporting the tight clustering around 32–34°C.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Taipei Songshan Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 17 Aug '26.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA) point to a daytime maximum of 35°C in Taipei on August 17, with mostly clear skies and a 20% chance of afternoon thundershowers.** This aligns with typical August conditions in the region, where highs average around 32–34°C amid high humidity and strong solar radiation.

Trader consensus splits narrowly between the 35°C (42%) and 36°C (37.5%) outcomes because minor variations in cloud cover, shower timing, or urban heat island effects could push the peak slightly higher or cap it lower. Afternoon convective activity often develops due to daytime heating and moisture, potentially limiting maximum temperatures through increased cloud shading or brief cooling. Historical August data shows occasional exceedances of 35°C under clear, stable high-pressure patterns, but recent model runs emphasize the risk of localized showers that could keep readings at or below the official forecast.

Upcoming CWA updates and refined numerical weather prediction outputs in the next 12–24 hours will likely clarify whether conditions trend toward full clearing or increased convective inhibition of the peak.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 17 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pa/panama-city/MPMG.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader sentiment for Panama City's highest temperature on August 17 centers on 30°C as the most probable outcome, reflecting typical wet-season conditions.** In Panama's equatorial climate, persistent high humidity, frequent convective showers from the Intertropical Convergence Zone, and cloud cover limit daytime heating, keeping highs near the long-term August average of 29–30°C. Recent model guidance shows no significant warming anomaly or clear-sky persistence that would push readings to 32°C or above, while the risk of heavier rain supports the 29°C and lower brackets. With resolution just hours away, these probabilities align with climatological baselines and current observational trends rather than unusual atmospheric patterns.
